result: The bug was entirely in the route pattern. `routes/web.ts:35` registered the archive as `/posts/archive/:date*`, but `*` is not a parameter modifier in the Hono router underneath `@guren/core` — it read the whole token as a parameter literally named `date*` that still matches only one segment. That produced exactly the two reported symptoms: `/posts/archive/2026` matched but handed the controller a `date*` key, so `ArchiveParamSchema` reported the required `date` missing (422), and `/posts/archive/2026/08` spanned two segments so nothing matched at all (404). I changed the pattern to `/posts/archive/:date{.+}` — the regex-constraint form the framework's own codegen already understands (`SegmentParamKey` and `substituteParams` in `.guren/routes.gen.ts` both strip `{…}` but have no handling for `*`) — and reran `bun run codegen` so `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` carry the corrected path. The controller, `ArchiveParamSchema`, and the route's `posts.archive` name are untouched, so nothing outside the archive changed. I also added a `posts.archive` block to `tests/PostController.test.ts` that migrates the test database, seeds four posts at fixed UTC timestamps in 1999–2000, and asserts the month listing (`/1999/03` and `/1999/3`), the year listing, newest-first ordering, `{"data":[]}` for an empty period, and 422s for months outside 1–12 and for malformed dates; `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (8 passing) both pass, and the tests are re-runnable against the persistent test DB.
